headline: Discussed resolution supporting House Bill 4087 on red-light cameras; no vote taken, and the bill was reported referred for study.
summary: The committee discussed a resolution supporting House Bill 4087 on traffic safety at intersections. The bill would let cities voluntarily use cameras to photograph red-light violations, with fines up to $300. No formal recommendation or vote was recorded.
decisions: Reported that House Bill 4087 was referred for study; no committee vote was recorded.

Public Portion 
 1. Discussion of the Resolution Supporting House Bill 4087, "An Act Relative to Traffic 
Safety at Intersections." 
On October 15, 2026, the Joint Maintenance & Development and Public Safety Committee, 
chaired by Councilors Lavar Click-Bruce and Gerry Martin, met to review the Resolution 
Supporting House Bill 4087, “An Act Relative to Traffic Safety at Intersections.” State 
Representative Orlando Ramos presented the proposed legislation, which would allow 
municipalities to voluntarily implement photographic cameras to identify red-light violations. 
Unlike Flock cameras, the proposed system would capture photographs of vehicles and license 
plates rather than continuously record video. Municipalities would decide whether to participate, 
set fines up to $300, and post warning signs. The system would issue citations to registered 
vehicle owners without insurance surcharges. The legislation would apply only to red-light 
violations, not speeding. 
 
The committee reviewed public safety concerns, implementation costs, potential grant funding, 
and the Springfield Police Department's role in reviewing violations and issuing citations. The 
Law Department recommended privacy safeguards limiting access, use, sharing, and retention of 
images, including prompt deletion of images unrelated to violations. Discussion also addressed 
the need for a local appeals process, including procedures for contesting citations, and the 
distinction between existing City cameras and privately operated license plate readers. 
 
Representative Ramos reported that the legislation had been referred for study and may be refiled 
if it is not passed during the current legislative session. Additional review of privacy protections, 
enforcement procedures, and appeals requirements was discussed, with further coordination 
involving the Police Department and Law Department. No formal recommendation or vote was 
recorded. The meeting adjourned at 5:38 p.m.
